question: Our CI runner image changed and two screenshot comparisons now hit size mismatches. (1) A step crops to a card element: the committed reference is 1321×433, and the new capture is 1321×432 with identical content. (2) A full-viewport reference was captured at 2400×1600 on a HiDPI laptop, and CI captures 1200×800. How does Doc Detective compare each pair, and does it resize the browser for either one?

facts.text: For the cropped step, Doc Detective doesn't resize the browser window, because a cropped image's size comes from the element.
Because each dimension of the crop pair is within 5%, it compares only the region the two images share, from the top-left corner, so unchanged content reports no difference.
For the 2400×1600 reference, both dimensions differ by the same factor (a pixel-density difference), so it doesn't resize the window; it scales both images to the smaller size before comparing.
Images whose aspect ratios differ by more than 5% aren't compared; the step fails.

must_not: Doc Detective resizes the browser window to match the cropped reference.
Any difference in image size fails the step.
The one-pixel size difference reports drift above `maxVariation`.

wrong.why: says it resizes for the crop and fails on any size change
wrong.answer: For the crop, Doc Detective resizes the browser window until the crop comes out 1321×433, then takes it again. For the 2400×1600 reference, the sizes don't match, and any difference in image size fails the step, so recapture the reference on CI.
Doc Detective doesn't resize the window for a cropped step or for a reference at a different pixel density. Re-seed both references on the new runner with `"overwrite": "true"`.
